scenes.title: What is Data Quality?
scenes.subtitle: Fitness of data for its intended use
scenes.narration: Data quality describes how well a dataset serves the decisions and processes that depend on it.

scenes.heading: Why data quality matters
bullets: Bad data drives wrong decisions and erodes trust in analytics
Downstream models and dashboards inherit every upstream defect
Regulatory reporting can fail when records are inaccurate
scenes.narration: Poor data leads teams to wrong conclusions, so quality problems are really decision problems, not just technical ones. Because pipelines flow forward, a single upstream defect silently corrupts every report and model downstream. And in regulated domains, inaccurate records expose the business to compliance and financial risk.

scenes.heading: How quality is judged
steps: Define fitness for a specific use case
Measure the data against that expectation
Compare results to a defined threshold
Act on the gap through fixes or alerts
scenes.narration: Quality is always judged relative to a purpose, so we first state what the data must be fit for. We then measure the actual data and compare it against an agreed threshold. When the gap is unacceptable, we remediate the source or raise an alert.

scenes.heading: Signals of poor quality
bullets: Missing or null values in required fields
Stale data that no longer reflects reality
scenes.narration: Nulls in mandatory fields break joins and calculations, so completeness is a frequent culprit. Duplicates quietly inflate totals and mislead the metrics people rely on. Stale data looks correct but describes a world that has already changed.

scenes.text: Data quality is fitness for use, measured against explicit expectations and acted on continuously.
scenes.narration: Treat quality as a measurable property tied to how the data is used, not a vague ideal. Define expectations, measure against them, and respond when reality drifts.
